Flagged txn 3506725 is $1,000.03 online (product R), 7.62x the 180d mean of $131.25 and above the card's all-time max of $670.04; amount_z 4.97.
Device 'Windows | Windows 10 | edge 16.0 | 1366x768' is new for this card (device_new_flag New, not among the 11 devices in 180d history) and the email domain is anonymous.com.

The same Edge device profile appears on six other cards in the rare-device link set (C00854-K2, C11309-K1, C11000-K2, C09241-K2, C08918-K2, C12690-K2), each with multiple confirmed fraud cases (account_takeover, card_not_present_new_device, out_of_region_use), indicating a shared compromise origin.
Only one transaction sits in the episode window and no card-testing or just-under-threshold runs exist, so exposure is confined to the single $1,000.03 authorization.

Prior case on this customer (CC-0873) cleared a 0.93-scored $50.05 txn after the cardholder confirmed travel; that benign precedent does not extend here because the cardholder now denies the charge and the device.

Policy R2 requires BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE on a denial, with FILE_REPORT since exposure exceeds $1,000 and the case connects to a shared device profile; R6 adds MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS for the shared element.

case.summary: Customer C10434 denies the $1,000.03 online purchase (txn 3506725) on card C10434-K1 and denies ever using a Windows Edge browser, which is the device recorded on the transaction and flagged New for the account. The amount is 7.62x the card's mean and above its all-time maximum, and the transaction carried an anonymous email domain. The same Edge device profile links to six other cards with extensive confirmed fraud histories, making this part of a shared-origin compromise rather than a one-off new-device purchase. Verdict: card-not-present fraud from a new device, strongly suspected. Recommend BLOCK_CARD and reissue, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT (exposure over $1,000 plus shared device profile), and MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS for the six linked cards.

sar.narrative: This report documents suspected card-not-present fraud committed from a new, unrecognized device against customer C10434 and card C10434-K1. On 2016-12-02 at 15:18:27, a single online purchase of $1,000.03 (product category R) was authorized on card C10434-K1 through the card-not-present channel. The transaction was recorded from device profile 'Windows | Windows 10 | edge 16.0 | 1366x768', which carried a device_new_flag of New and did not match any of the 11 devices seen in the card's prior 180-day history, and it was submitted with an email address on the anonymous.com domain. The amount is 7.62 times the card's 180-day mean of $131.25, exceeds the card's all-time maximum of $670.04, and carries an amount_z score of 4.97. When contacted for validation, the cardholder denied making the purchase, stated they have never used a Windows Edge browser because their devices are an iPhone, a Mac and a Chrome laptop, and confirmed they have never spent near that amount on this card; they requested that the card be blocked and reissued. Graph review established that the same Edge device profile appears on six other cards, C00854-K2, C11309-K1, C11000-K2, C09241-K2, C08918-K2 and C12690-K2, each of which carries multiple confirmed fraud cases including account takeover, card-not-present new-device use, and out-of-region use, indicating a shared compromise origin rather than an isolated new-device purchase. A prior case on this customer, CC-0873, cleared a similarly scored $50.05 transaction after the cardholder confirmed travel, but that benign precedent does not apply here because the cardholder now denies both the charge and the device. Only one transaction falls within the episode window, with no card-testing runs or just-under-threshold sequences, so total exposure is confined to $1,000.03. The activity is reported as suspicious because an unrecognized device tied to a multi-card fraud cluster, an anonymized email domain, a record-high transaction amount, and a direct customer denial converge on the same authorization. The bank blocked and reissued card C10434-K1, opened a fraud case, placed the six linked cards under monitoring for the shared device profile, and is filing this report as exposure exceeds $1,000 and the case connects to a shared device profile.

stop_reason: Decisive: p=0.93 with 4 independent signals and evidence confidence 0.70 (policy §6). Verification response settled the question: probability 0.93 with four independent signals (denial, amount above card max, new device absent from history, shared device profile across confirmed-fraud cards); further evidence would not change the decision.
